name: bfs-attributes
description: A text file on BFS that carries three typed extended attributes (a string, an int32 and a MIME type). The agent is asked to make an ordinary two-line edit to its contents.
proves: that editing a file preserves its BFS attributes. A write that goes through a temporary file and a rename — the usual way to make a write atomic — drops every attribute unless they are carried across deliberately, and on Haiku that silently breaks packaging, indexing and Tracker.
notes: Haiku only. Off Haiku there is no addattr/catattr/listattr and the task reports n/a — a filesystem this machine does not have is not a failure of either agent. The attributes are set by setup_commands because a fixture directory in git cannot carry them.
prompt: In `docs/manual.txt`, change the line `Version: 1.2` to `Version: 1.3` and add a line `Status: released` directly underneath it. Leave the rest of the file exactly as it is.
